# 'seaimp' Dialect

_Imperative layer over sea: variables, lowered to sea._

`seaimp` holds what is convenient to write but not SSA: variables
(`seaimp.var`, read and written whole by `seaimp.get` / `seaimp.set`).
It has no runtime semantics of its own: a program means what its
lowering to sea means (`sea-lower-seaimp`, MLIR's Mem2Reg). The
interpreter and the VC generator refuse seaimp ops
(docs/design/SeaImp.md).

[TOC]

## Operations

### `seaimp.get` (::sea::imp::GetOp)

_Read a variable_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `seaimp.get` $var attr-dict `:` qualified(type($var))
```

The value the variable holds: the last `seaimp.set` before it on the
path, or the variable's initial value.

```mlir
%v = seaimp.get %x : !seaimp.var<i32>
```

Interfaces: `PromotableMemOpInterface`

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `var` | seaimp variable handle |

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | any non-token type |



### `seaimp.set` (::sea::imp::SetOp)

_Write a variable_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `seaimp.set` $var `,` $value attr-dict `:` qualified(type($var))
```

Replaces the value the variable holds.

```mlir
seaimp.set %x, %v : !seaimp.var<i32>
```

Interfaces: `PromotableMemOpInterface`

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `var` | seaimp variable handle |
| `value` | any non-token type |



### `seaimp.var` (::sea::imp::VarOp)

_Declare a variable_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `seaimp.var` $name ` ` `[` $site `]` attr-dict `:` qualified(type($result))
```

A variable holding one value of type `T`, read and written whole. A
read before any write gives the variable's initial value, one
nondeterministic value named by `name` and `site`: the lowering makes
it `sea.nondet "<name>" [<site>]` (integers), `sea.struct.nondet`
(structs: one bit-vector of the integer and address leaves, pointer
leaves null) or `sea.ptr.nondet` (pointers: never dereferenceable).
Every read before a write sees the same value. `site` is unique with
the program's other nondet sites.

The op is in the entry block of a `sea.program`. Its result is used
only as the variable operand of `seaimp.get` / `seaimp.set` in the
same region (not as a block argument, a select operand or a stored
value): every verified variable is promoted by the lowering.

```mlir
%x = seaimp.var "x" [7] : !seaimp.var<i32>
```

Interfaces: `PromotableAllocationOpInterface`, `Sea_NondetSiteOpInterface`

#### Attributes:

<table>
<tr><th>Attribute</th><th>MLIR Type</th><th>Description</th></tr>
<tr><td><code>name</code></td><td>::mlir::StringAttr</td><td>string attribute</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>site</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>64-bit signless integer attribute whose value is non-negative</td></tr>
</table>

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | seaimp variable handle |



## Types

### VarType

_A handle to a variable holding a value of type `T`_

Syntax:

```
!seaimp.var<
  ::mlir::Type   # valueType
>
```

The handle of a `seaimp.var`. It is not a program value: only
`seaimp.get` and `seaimp.set` may use it. `T` is a sea register type:
a signless integer, a pointer (`!sea.ptr`) or a struct
(`!sea.struct`). Addresses and memories are not supported yet.

```mlir
!seaimp.var<i32>
!seaimp.var<!sea.ptr<64>>
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| valueType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
